fix: Reuse the previous empty scope instead of allocating two Rc cells on every build. Hoist `let previous = node.child_scope.borrow().clone();` above the `let scope = ...` statement and replace the `else if` arm with `} else if spec.enter.is_some() { match previous { Some(scope) if scope.stagger.is_none() => Some(scope), _ => Some(StaggerScope::empty()) } }`. An empty scope carries no per-build state: stagger_delay returns early when stagger is None.
Use `let count = child.kind().structure().children.into_iter().len();`. WidgetChildrenIter implements ExactSizeIterator, so this is O(1) instead of walking the children.

Stop cloning the whole item Vec on every call. Keep the `retain` (it needs borrow_mut), then have `ordered` and `relax`/`arrange` iterate `self.items.borrow().iter()` directly, cloning only the Rc of items they keep (`ordered` already filters by list). If a Ref cannot be held across the animate calls, filter into a scratch buffer stored on Core and clear it instead of allocating. live_items is reached per drag step through ordered, index_of, plan, locate and arrange, so this allocates several times per pointer move.

Compute the average without allocating: `let (sum, count) = original.windows(2).fold((0., 0usize), |(sum, count), pair| { let gap = match axis { Flow::Horizontal => pair[1].origin.x - (pair[0].origin.x + pair[0].size.width), _ => pair[1].origin.y - (pair[0].origin.y + pair[0].size.height) }; (sum + gap, count + 1) }); if count == 0 { 0. } else { sum / count as f32 }`. Same summation order, so results are identical. restack runs on every drag step through plan.

Collect is only passed as a slice to flow_of. Make flow_of take `impl Iterator<Item = Rect> + Clone` (or pass a precomputed rect slice from a scratch buffer) so the Vec<Rect> is not allocated. flow_of reads rects[0] and calls .all() twice, so rewrite it with `let mut rects = rects; let first = rects.next()?` style or a `first()` on a clone. Called on every locate, i.e. every drag step.

arrange scans the whole plan for every live item (O(items x plan) per drag step). Store the target on Item as a `Cell<Offset>`: reset every live item's target to Offset::ZERO, then assign each planned origin in one pass over `plan` (`for (item, rect, origin) in &plan { item.target.set(*origin - rect.origin) }`), and read `item.target.get()` in the loop. finish() has the same find for the dropped item and can read the same field.
